clock_alignment.alignment_procedure: Raw pgbench transaction logs record microsecond gettimeofday() epoch timestamps; resource monitor records UTC ISO8601 wall timestamps and CLOCK_MONOTONIC. Synchronization is achieved by matching UTC epoch timestamps.

cfs_throttling_analysis.multi_task_aggregate_explanation: cgroup v2 cpu.stat throttled_usec represents the sum of execution time during which runnable threads in the cgroup were withheld from CPU execution due to quota exhaustion. Because PostgreSQL runs multiple backend threads/processes (8 active client connections plus postmaster, checkpointer, bgwriter, and walwriter), multiple threads can be throttled simultaneously within each 100ms CFS quota period. Consequently, aggregate throttled_usec accumulates across concurrent tasks and can mathematically exceed elapsed wall-clock duration.
methodological_guardrails: throttled_usec must NEVER be interpreted as individual request wait time or client perceived latency.
throttled_usec must NEVER be divided by client connection count (e.g. 8) to claim average client stall time.
throttled_usec must NEVER be converted to a percentage of benchmark duration without explicitly noting multi-task aggregation.
